claim_text: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
audit_scope: This audit verifies numerical consistency and evidential support for the OT-loss/refinement claim from Table 4 (p.8) after FAUST+SCAPE training, tested on SHREC19. It does NOT re-run training, verify code execution or Sinkhorn convergence, assess statistical significance/variance, validate fmap/proper loss weights (lambda1, lambda3 not ablated), or claim generalization beyond SHREC19 or to present-day SOTA.

methodology_findings.finding: Eq.10 LbiSW definition is verified as bidirectional sum (E_theta~U(Sd-1)[Wp^p(theta]Fx, theta]hatFy)+Wp^p(theta]Fy, theta]hatFx)])^{1/p} with soft permutations hatFx=hatPi_yx Fx, hatFy=hatPi_xy Fy per Eq.9, but 'necessary for best accuracy' rests on 0.1-0.2 delta (LuniSW 4.9, LbiSW 4.8, Ours 4.7) without variance or significance.
methodology_findings.evidence: Eq.10 text: LbiSW = (E_theta~U(Sd-1)[Wp^p(theta]Fx, theta]hatFy)+Wp^p(theta]Fy, theta]hatFx)])^{1/p} where hatFx=hatPi_yxFx and hatFy=hatPi_xyFy; Table 4: w. LuniSW 4.9, w. LbiSW 4.8, Ours 4.7

methodology_findings.finding: Eq.11 LbiEBSW shared importance-sampling is verified with shared sigma0(theta) and weight w(theta)=exp(W_X+W_Y)/sigma0(theta), but Table 4 body does not numerically separate biEBSW; attribution relies on text 'last row indicates that by employing importance sampling energy-based SW, we can even gain better performance' implying Ours=biEBSW at 4.7 vs LbiSW 4.8 delta 0.1.
methodology_findings.evidence: Eq.11: LbiEBSW = [E_theta~sigma0[(W_theta,X+W_theta,Y) w(theta)] / E_theta~sigma0[w(theta)]]^{1/p} where w(theta)=exp(W_theta,X+W_theta,Y)/sigma0(theta); Table 4 limitations: does not separate biEBSW number in table body beyond text; p.8 Results: 'the last row indicates that by employing importance sampling energy-based SW, we can even gain better performance'

methodology_findings.finding: Eq.14 adaptive refinement is defined as iterated Sinkhorn projections ~Pi_xy = QX(QY...(QX(p_eps))) with p_eps ~ exp(-1/eps c^2), but bundle states it is used once at inference due to quadratic memory, not during training. 'Not using adaptive refinement at end of training' (Table 4 caption) conflates inference-time refinement effect (4.7 vs 7.2) with OT-loss training effect.
methodology_findings.evidence: Eq.14: ~Pi_xy = QX(QY...(QX(p_eps))) where Q(.) projection of p_eps(x,y)/exp(-1/eps c^2(x,y)); p.6 Sec4.5: 'we only employ entropic OT for refinement once during the inference, thereby reducing computation and memory cost' and Limitations: 'Used only once at inference due to quadratic memory; not used for large-scale training'; Table 4 caption: 'fourth row indicates not using adaptive refinement at the end of the training process' with w.o. adaptive refinement 7.2 vs Ours 4.7

methodology_findings.finding: Ablation manipulates LOT type and refinement presence but does not report/control lambda_fmap/lambda_proper weights in Ltotal=lambda1 Lfmap+lambda2 LOT+lambda3 Lproper, random seeds, optimizer schedule, tau scaling, or Sinkhorn epsilon/iterations; no ablation of proper/fmap terms.
methodology_findings.evidence: Eq.13: Ltotal = lambda1 Lfmap + lambda2 LOT + lambda3 Lproper where lambdai is weight, LOT could be either LbiSW or LbiEBSW; Claim limitations: 'Ablation only on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training; does not ablate proper or fmap weights'; Table 4: Ablation over OT loss variants and adaptive refinement

methodology_findings.finding: Protocol is single train-test split: train on FAUST+SCAPE, test on SHREC19 (44 shapes, 430 pairs). No cross-validation, no separate validation split described, no multi-dataset ablation. Author-stated limitation acknowledges this scope.
methodology_findings.evidence: p.8 Settings: 'We train our model on FAUST+SCAPE dataset and evaluate it on SHREC19 dataset'; Claim limitations: 'Ablation only on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training'; Gaps: 'section-level retrieval unavailable; audit uses object evidence plus page excerpts only'

methodology_findings.finding: No uncertainty intervals, variance across seeds, statistical tests, or cross-validation reported for deltas 4.9->4.8->4.7 or 7.2->4.7. Single-point mean geodesic errors do not support necessity claim across hyperparameters/datasets.
methodology_findings.evidence: Table 4 values: w. LMSE 34.3, w. LuniSW 4.9, w. LbiSW 4.8, w.o. adaptive refinement 7.2, Ours 4.7 with no variance, CI, or seed information; Gaps: no methods/limitations sections available beyond excerpts

methodology_findings.finding: Large LMSE degradation (34.3 vs 4.7) may reflect mismatched scaling/temperature tau in Eq.9, loss weighting lambda2, or lack of tuning rather than intrinsic inability of MSE to align features; no LMSE hyperparameter search reported.
methodology_findings.evidence: Eq.9 soft similarity: hatPi_i,j = exp((Fi_x · Fj_y)/tau) / sum_k exp((Fi_x · Fk_y)/tau) where tau is scaling factor; Table 4: w. LMSE 34.3 vs Ours 4.7; p.8 text: 'LMSE can not learn to align features for retrieving p2p correspondence' without tuning details

methodology_findings.finding: Causal claim of necessity overreaches: ablation shows association on one benchmark, but does not control confounders (properness/bijection regularization, feature extractor capacity) and does not disentangle double-counting where Ltotal is minimized both during training (via LOT) and during refinement (via differentiable Sinkhorn updating features to minimize Ltotal).
methodology_findings.evidence: Ltotal = lambda1 Lfmap + lambda2 LOT + lambda3 Lproper; p.6: 'Thanks to differentiable property of Sinkhorn algorithm, we can refine each individual pair by minimizing the Ltotal to update the features accordingly'; p.6 Eq.14 adaptive refinement paragraph notes orthogonal to [18] and reduces cost by using once at inference

methodology_findings.finding: Reproducibility details absent in bundle: lambda1/2/3 values, tau, eps (entropic regularizer), Sinkhorn iterations, optimizer/LR/schedule, number of slices for SW/EBSW, seeds, and validation procedure. Metric comparability relies on external citation for mean geodesic error (x100) without re-derivation of normalization.
methodology_findings.evidence: Metrics: 'we employ mean geodesic errors (x100) [25]'; Eq.13 lambdai weights not enumerated; Eq.9 tau scaling factor not quantified; Gaps: section-level retrieval unavailable

methodology_findings.finding: Authors explicitly note refinement limited to once at inference due to quadratic memory and ablation limited to SHREC19 without proper/fmap weight ablation, consistent with audit that efficacy claim is scoped to single dataset/split.
methodology_findings.evidence: Limitations: 'Used only once at inference due to quadratic memory; not used for large-scale training' and 'Trained on FAUST+SCAPE, tested only on SHREC19; does not separate biEBSW number in table body beyond text' and 'does not ablate proper or fmap weights'

cross_paper_findings.detail: Both use entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy to enable differentiable Sinkhorn optimization (Eq.8 vs claim Eq.14). This supports general plausibility of entropic OT/Sinkhorn mechanism underlying refinement efficacy, but f1 concerns shape-matching OT energy, not LOT vs MSE ablation or 4.7-to-7.2 refinement degradation. Ground-cost space differs (product embedding R^{K+6} per f4 vs feature Rd for claim) blocking direct numeric comparison. f1 contains no evidence on bidirectional cycle-consistency motivation in Eq.10 or OT plan vs functional map coupling to assess orthogonal contribution.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 8: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization

cross_paper_findings.detail: Direct mechanistic alignment on Gibbs density encoding: Eq.10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input, same construction as claim Eq.14 (p_lambda from squared embedding/feature distance). However ground cost space differs (product-embedding distance per f2/f4 vs feature distance for claim), as flagged in comparison target, so costs are not identical. f2 provides no test of replacing LOT with MSE or removing refinement, so cannot confirm/contradict 'degrades drastically' or '4.7 to 7.2' necessity. No evidence on bidirectional cycle-consistency alignment or functional map coupling.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input

cross_paper_findings.detail: f3 shows second OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial soft correspondences (Eq.13), exemplifying alternative ground cost in same pipeline. This demonstrates feature-space OT viability, consistent in principle with claim's feature-space refinement, but role differs: deep-shells uses feature-distance OT for initialization vs claim uses OT (Eq.14) for entropic adaptive refinement. Role difference means 'refinement necessity' (4.7-7.2 degradation) vs alternative initialization role cannot be directly compared; f3 does not test LOT vs MSE or refinement removal, and provides no bidirectional cycle-consistency or OT vs functional map coupling discussion to assess orthogonal contribution.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 13: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi, showing alternative ground cost in same pipeline

cross_paper_findings.detail: f4 explicitly defines product-space embedding of shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates/normals where Euclidean distance serves as OT ground cost (Eq.3). This directly evidences the space difference in comparison target: product embedding R^{K+6} vs claim's feature Rd for ground cost. Embedding choice shows OT ground-cost construction is space-dependent, so cannot confirm/contradict refinement necessity quantitative claim or LOT vs MSE degradation. f4 provides no ablation numbers and no discussion of bidirectional cycle-consistency motivation or functional map coupling for orthogonal contribution assessment.
cross_paper_findings.evidence: Eq. 3 embeds shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals whose Euclidean distance becomes ground cost
